Assertions.Description: The Keyboard Manager Settings entry opens the configured usable editor.
With new editor selected and module enabled, the configured editor shortcut opens it through actual keyboard input.
With new editor selected and module enabled, Dashboard lists its configured editor shortcut.
With the installed PowerToys Command Palette integration, its open-editor command opens the new editor.
With Dock integration available and owned pin restoration, pin and relaunch the new editor command from the Dock.
Clearing the editor shortcut stops its old binding from opening the editor; restoring it restores activation. The removed separate service-toggle shortcut is not required.
Settings switches between new editor and both classic remap windows without losing mappings.
Reopening retains the explicitly selected editor preference and original preference is restored.
In an authorized isolated clean/migration fixture, absent useNewEditor selects the new editor.
In an authorized isolated migration fixture, explicitly false useNewEditor remains classic.
Classic Remap keys adds and removes rows through its corresponding buttons.
Classic OK with blank rows shows the invalid-mappings warning.
Classic Remap keys OK saves valid owned mappings and reopening loads them.
Classic Remap shortcuts OK saves valid owned mappings and reopening loads them.
Saving a valid owned key mapping in the new editor shows the list entry and corresponding persisted engine and editor entries.
Closing and reopening the owned new editor retains the saved owned mapping in the list and both stores.
Canceling an unsaved add and an unsaved edit leaves the original stored mappings unchanged.
An empty new-editor mapping draft cannot commit an invalid mapping.
Using Type only, classic Remap keys source accepts keys rather than shortcuts.
Using Type only, classic Remap shortcuts source accepts shortcuts rather than standalone keys.
Using Type only in each classic window, its target accepts both keys and shortcuts.
In each classic Type dialog, holding Enter accepts the recorded input.
In each classic Type dialog, holding Escape cancels without committing the draft.
New editor trigger and action fields record their requested keys/shortcuts.
New-editor recorded modifiers display Win, Ctrl, Alt, Shift, action regardless of press order.
On builds with editor-scoped recording, owned text typed in another foreground process is not recorded.
On builds with recording focus exit, lone Tab ends recording, retains captured keys, unchecks recording and moves focus forward.
On builds with recording focus exit, Shift+Tab ends recording, retains captured keys, unchecks recording and moves focus backward.
Stopping new-editor recording without capturing keys restores the previous keys; lone Tab remains selectable through the dropdown.
Dropdowns create key-to-key mappings using mouse selection and, independently, keyboard navigation.
Dropdowns create key-to-shortcut mappings using mouse selection and, independently, keyboard navigation.
Dropdowns create shortcut-to-key mappings using mouse selection and, independently, keyboard navigation.
Dropdowns create shortcut-to-shortcut mappings using mouse selection and, independently, keyboard navigation.
On builds with empty-slot pickers, both empty fields offer Select key; a media key is selectable without pressing it and a selected modifier adds a slot for building a shortcut.
Key search is case-insensitive, Enter selects a match, no matches show an explicit state and reopening clears search.
Invalid selection reverts without breaking later dropdown updates; placeholder/None is never persisted as a key.
Adding a duplicate mapping is rejected without changing the saved original.
Editing an owned entry into another entry's identity/conflict is rejected without changing the saved original.
Always and Alone entries for the same key are treated as distinct identities.
Distinct left/right modifier mappings are allowed; conflicting generic-versus-specific variants are rejected.
Disable actions enforce valid nonempty triggers and duplicate/modifier-conflict rules.
Dropdown-created Win+L and Win+Ctrl+L sources and targets are rejected without physically injecting a workstation-lock gesture.
With an owned A to B mapping and ordinary text fixture, press/release A produces B instead of A and subsequent input is not left modified.
Holding/repeating A with A to B produces repeated target input without A leakage or stuck input after release.
Ctrl to A press/release produces A; exercise applicable modifier/action release orders and verify ordinary input afterward.
Ctrl to A held/repeated input produces the target without residual Ctrl, including applicable release orders.
A to Ctrl press/release provides target Ctrl behavior in an owned observer, with applicable release orders and no stuck modifier.
A to Ctrl held input participates in the target modifier combination and releases correctly in both orders.
Win to B press/release produces B without accidentally opening Start or leaving a modifier held.
Win to B held/repeated input produces the target without source Start leakage, including applicable release orders.
B to Win press/release produces intended target-Win behavior without an additional accidental Start activation; observe target key state.
B to Win held input participates in intended Win combinations, with both release orders and no accidental additional Start activation.
A to Disable suppresses a press/release A in an owned text/key observer and normal input afterward works.
A to Disable suppresses held/repeated A input and leaves no stuck state.
Win to Disable suppresses press/release without opening Start or leaving a modifier held.
Win to Disable suppresses held/repeated input without Start leakage or stuck modifiers; exercise applicable release orders.
A to Ctrl+V press/release pastes protected synthetic text instead of A, with no residual modifiers.
A to Ctrl+V held/repeated input performs target paste behavior and releases target modifiers correctly.
B to Win+A press/release invokes Quick Settings rather than B, with owned shell-surface cleanup.
B to Win+A held/repeated input routes to the target, releases modifiers correctly and does not leak B.
Ctrl+A to Ctrl+V taps paste synthetic text instead of Select all; exercise modifier-first and action-first release orders.
Ctrl+A to Ctrl+V held/repeated input and both release orders preserve target behavior without stuck modifiers.
Win+A to Ctrl+V taps paste synthetic text instead of Quick Settings; both release orders leave ordinary input working.
Win+A to Ctrl+V held/repeated input and both release orders preserve target paste behavior without shell leakage.
Ctrl+V to Win+A taps open the intended Windows surface rather than paste; test both release orders.
Ctrl+V to Win+A held/repeated input and both release orders preserve target behavior without stuck modifiers.
With Feedback Hub installed and owned activation/closure, Win+A to Win+F taps open the intended target instead of Quick Settings, with both release orders.
With Feedback Hub and owned lifecycle available, Win+A to Win+F held/repeated input and both release orders route correctly and restore ordinary input.
Ctrl+A to B taps produce B rather than Select all, with both modifier/action release orders.
Ctrl+A to B held/repeated input produces the target and both release orders leave no stuck modifiers.
Ctrl+A to Win taps produce target-Win behavior in an owned key/Start observer, with both release orders and no extra source action.
Ctrl+A to Win held input and both release orders produce intended target combinations without stuck modifiers.
Win+A to B taps produce B rather than Quick Settings, with both release orders.
Win+A to B held/repeated input and both release orders preserve target behavior without shell leakage or stuck modifiers.
With an owned Edge fixture targeted as msedge, applicable shortcut matrix rows work only in that foreground app, including tap/hold/release-order conditions.
With an owned VS Code fixture targeted as code, applicable shortcut matrix rows work only in that foreground app, including tap/hold/release-order conditions.
With owned non-admin cmd in Windows Terminal targeted as windowsterminal, applicable shortcut matrix rows work only in that foreground app, including tap/hold/release orders.
Requires authorized elevated PowerToys and elevated cmd in Windows Terminal: applicable app-specific shortcut matrix rows work with tap/hold/release-order coverage; unrelated apps remain unaffected.
An app-specific Alt+Tab target in owned fixtures changes focus without stuck modifiers or subsequent remaps going to the wrong application.
An app-specific Alt+F4 target closes only an owned window and leaves subsequent input/remap routing correct.
Hold Ctrl across D then E with Ctrl+D to Ctrl+A and Ctrl+E to Ctrl+V: select all then paste synthetic text; after release ordinary typing works.
Hold Win across D then E with Win+D to Ctrl+A and Win+E to Ctrl+V: select all then paste synthetic text without source shell actions; ordinary input works after release.
Settings module disable/re-enable stops/resumes mapping behavior without losing saved rows; restore original enabled state.
An owned key/shortcut remap row stops/resumes when toggled off/on; deleting it while disabled remains absent after reopen, preserving other entries.
An owned text row stops/resumes when toggled off/on; deleting it while disabled remains absent after reopen, preserving other entries.
An owned program row stops/resumes when toggled off/on; deleting it while disabled remains absent after reopen, preserving other entries and launched-process ownership.
An owned URL row stops/resumes when toggled off/on; deleting it while disabled remains absent after reopen, preserving other entries and browser state.
Deleting an enabled owned key mapping removes it from both stores and immediately restores ordinary source-key input without changing other entries.
A saved/reopened key-to-text mapping inserts exact synthetic single-line text.
A saved/reopened shortcut-to-text mapping inserts exact synthetic single-line text.
Multiline replacement preserves requested line breaks in an owned editor and does not submit an owned chat-style fixture.
Whitespace-only text is accepted, persisted and inserted exactly rather than rejected as empty.
Consecutive activations insert each requested replacement without drops, duplicates or engine crash.
Single-key text replacement still inserts while Alt is held, without unintended menu activation or stuck Alt afterward.
Single-key text replacement while Win is held inserts text without accidental Start activation or stuck Win afterward.
Single-key text replacement while Ctrl is held inserts text and does not leave released Ctrl stuck.
Single-key text replacement while Shift is held inserts text and does not leave released Shift stuck.
A saved Run program mapping launches an owned harmless executable with requested arguments and actual ordinary process context.
With installed handlers and owned resources, .lnk, app execution alias and associated-file mappings each launch their intended targets.
An executable uses its containing directory for blank Start in, honors explicit valid Start in and rejects an invalid configured directory.
Requires authorized elevated PowerToys: Normal visible executable and supported Shell targets launch non-elevated, verified on actual target tokens.
Requires authorized elevated editor: both program-file and Start in folder pickers open, support selection and support cancellation.
Requires authorized elevation: explicitly Elevated mappings retain their intended elevated launch behavior and owned-process cleanup.
Requires an authorized alternative account and credential-entry path: Different user retains its selected account context without disclosing credentials.
With an owned harmless process and explicit hidden-lifetime observer, Hidden launches preserve intended hidden-window behavior.
A saved/reopened URL mapping opens the approved synthetic URL in its configured handler, with owned tab/window cleanup.
Empty/invalid URL input cannot commit a valid URL mapping or replace the original saved entry.
On a supporting build, single-key to key/shortcut Alone condition and list badge survive save/reopen.
Solo release fires its target once, including after a long hold; no timeout-based cancellation is assumed.
Combining a held Alone source with another key preserves original modifier combination and suppresses the solo action.
With an owned mouse-capable fixture, combining a held Alone source with a button preserves the modifier-click and suppresses the solo action.
With an owned wheel observer, combining a held Alone source with wheel input preserves the modified wheel action and suppresses the solo action.
Mouse movement alone while the Alone source is held does not cancel its release-triggered solo action.
The condition control is unavailable for unsupported text/program/URL actions; left/right sources and an Always sibling retain distinct entries.
Case-insensitive substring search matches owned key names, replacement text, URL, program path and target app.
Win/Ctrl/Alt/Shift filters use trigger modifiers and multiple selected modifiers combine with OR.
All apps, Global only and a named app produce the corresponding owned rows.
Text, modifier and app categories combine with AND.
No matches exposes Clear filters, differs from an empty configuration, and clearing restores all owned rows.
Filtering does not mutate persisted mappings or become persisted configuration.
Select mode counts selected visible rows across sections; canceling selection preserves all rows.
Canceling the bulk delete confirmation preserves every saved row.
Confirming deletes only selected visible rows from UI and both stores, preserving hidden and unselected rows.
Reopening retains the bulk deletion and surviving entries before owned-fixture restoration.
With an installed AltGr layout, press/release AltGr outside a remap then use LCtrl+Y to Backspace; subsequent typing proves Ctrl is not stuck.
An AltGr-based shortcut still works with the installed layout and owned observer.
Ordinary AltGr character input, such as German AltGr+Q, remains correct; restore original layout/composition state.
Left Alt to Backspace tap deletes one character in known owned text, not an unintended Alt+Backspace/whole-word action.
Left Alt to Backspace held input repeats intended deletion and leaves no Alt/menu state after release; message-level evidence distinguishes unintended system-key delivery where available.
In a provisioned non-English Windows-language fixture, applicable classic/new editor controls, dialogs and tooltips localize; restore original language.
An authorized live light/dark theme switch updates the new editor title bar without corrupting mappings; restore the original theme.
In an authorized isolated DSC v3 fixture, KeyboardManagerProfile get/test/export/schema/manifest expose the declared profile resource and friendly layout-invariant key names.
Authorized isolated set replaces the whole profile containing key, Disable, text, chord, app-specific and exact-match entries; test becomes true and entries round-trip.
Authorized isolated deployment reloads the running engine without restarting PowerToys and editor/engine stores agree.

Only with diagnostic consent and supported normal-restart preservation, enable collection/viewing, restart, exercise Keyboard Manager and observe corresponding XML events in Diagnostic data viewer; restore original diagnostic state.
